# S261 — Shared role matrix: apply ork's matrix to one project or to every registered project

*Proposed.* The owner tells ork to copy the role matrix of one registered project (ork's own, as the owner asked) to another registered project, or to every registered project at once, so that the matrices unify. ork reads both matrices with `slicer relay-roles show --json`, builds a whole-matrix change set that keeps each target's own spec-check row and rule and its UI-pass row and rule, rewrites the row ids that copied rule text names to the target's ids, and writes it through slicer's atomic `relay-roles apply` replace form (S250, slicer s443 and s444) after a dry run the owner confirms per project. The design is open: see `Open owner questions`; ask the owner before the relay starts. The command and method names below (`ork roles matrix copy`, `matrix.copy`) are *proposed* and part of Q7.

**Findings:** Owner 2026-11-03: the owner should be able to tell ork to apply its relay roles matrix to any project so the matrices unify, or to all registered projects at once. Facts (read with slicer relay-roles show, 2026-11-03): the matrices differ per project. ork has 20 rows and 3 gpt-6.1-sol rows; slicer 18 and 5; daystar 12 and 2; adjudicate 9, pitfight 8 and squalify 8 have no Codex rows. slicer owns the matrix (.slicer/relay-roles.json, changed only through slicer relay-roles commands); S173 edits one project row by row, S250 applies a change set atomically through a proposed slicer relay-roles apply. Needed first: check that slicer has no such capability or roadmap item, then spec it with owner questions: the source (ork's own project matrix or a stored master), what is copied (rows, rules, or both), project-specific rows to keep (the spec-check row and rule, notes), dry run and per-project confirm, and the apply-to-all mode. Spec being drafted by an Opus medium subagent. · **Size:** M · **Tree:**

**Not in this slice:** a TUI action (a later item on S226 or S251); a master matrix stored by ork; any edit of .slicer/relay-roles.json other than through slicer relay-roles apply; committing the change; merging rows; any change to how plans read the matrix (internal/daemon/runs.go); new slicer commands (s443 and s444 are slicer's); the agents repo.

## Why

Owner, 2026-11-03: the owner should be able to tell ork to apply its own relay roles matrix to any registered project, so the project matrices unify, or to all registered projects at once.

Facts read on 2026-11-03:
- The matrices differ per project. `slicer relay-roles show --json --root DIR`: ork has 26 rows after commit f3d34f9 (3 gpt-6.1-sol and 6 gpt-6.1-terra Codex rows, 4 Grok rows with model `latest`) and rules u1, u3-u11; slicer has 18 rows (5 gpt-6.1-sol rows, 3 Grok rows pinned to `grok-4.7`) and rules u1-u10; adjudicate has 9 rows, no Codex row, and keeps rule u2 "No cross-vendor reviewer unless the owner asks", which ork dropped today (f3d34f9). The owner's figures for daystar (12 rows, 2 sol), pitfight (8) and squalify (8) were not re-read here: those repos are outside this workspace.
- Row ids and rule ids differ per project, and the same id means different things: the Spec check row is r16 in ork (rule u11), r18 in slicer (rule u10) and r9 in adjudicate (rule u6); rule u2 bars a cross-vendor reviewer in adjudicate and allows one in slicer.
- Rule text names row ids. ork's u8 names r8, r4, r9, r12, r15 and r3; u10 names r14; u11 names r16 and r14. A row copied to another project gets a new id there, so copied rule text must be rewritten, or it points at the wrong row.
- Some rules are ork-specific: u10 names `internal/tui`, `docs/dashboard.md` and the skills enabled in ork's `.claude/settings.json`; u7 names record 124 and `ork run PARENT --slivers`. Some rows carry project notes (adjudicate r1, r2, r4: "owner 2026-10-15: Haiku replaced after sandbox-rul...").
- ork reads the spec-check and UI-pass rows only through rule text: `SpecCheckRowID` matches `Spec check row \((r\d+)\)` and `UIPassRowID` matches `UI pass row \((r\d+)\)` (`internal/slicercli/write.go:240-266`). `planRun` drops both rows from the reviewer and gate chains (`internal/daemon/runs.go:386-424`), and the spec check refuses a matrix without that rule (`internal/daemon/speccheck.go:94-96`). A unified matrix must keep a spec-check row and a rule that names its id in that project.
- ork's `slicercli.Row` has no condition fields (`internal/slicercli/types.go:214-222`), while `show --json` gives each row a `when` object (size, effort, importance, urgency, well_specified, split, sliver). Copying a row needs `when`.
- `matrixAdapters` maps only `claude code` and `codex` (`internal/daemon/runs.go:345-346`, adj 155); Grok rows are skipped by ork's plans but used by relays that ork does not run.

slicer (checked as AGENTS.md asks, `slicer find` in ../slicer on 2026-11-03 for matrix, relay-roles, relay roles, apply, replace, copy, sync, template, global, user-level, default matrix, shared matrix, master):
- No slicer command copies or unifies a matrix across projects, and no item plans one. slicer s443 (`relay-roles-apply`, open, v1.20) names "a user-level (global) default matrix" under Not in this slice.
- slicer s444 (`relay-roles-replace`, open, v1.20, depends on s443) is the write primitive this slice needs: a complete matrix that replaces the current one in one atomic, validated write with `expect` and `--dry-run`; its Why says "A tool can copy a matrix from one project to another". Its rules: a row or rule with an `id` must exist in the target (else `unknown_role_row` or `unknown_role_rule`); one without `id` is added with the next id; absent ids are removed; rules have no move verb, so a replace whose rule order the derived steps cannot reach is refused with `usage`. Its test `test_RelayRolesApply_Replace_FromAnotherProject` covers rows of project A without their ids replaced into B.
- The installed slicer is 1.18.0, which has no `relay-roles apply` (`slicer relay-roles --help` lists show, recommend, init, add, set, remove, move, rule-add, rule-edit, rule-remove).

ork items: S250 (`matrix-apply`, open, v1.2) passes a change set, `ops` or `replace`, to `slicer relay-roles apply` for one project and returns slicer's result with adapter warnings; S173 (`matrix.edit`, open, v1.1) runs one `relay-roles` verb per call; S226 (matrix editor in the TUI, depends on S173) and S251 (project settings pane) are the TUI places. None of them copies a matrix between projects. This slice builds on S250's `RelayRolesApply` client call.

No adj question is filed by this draft; the owner questions are below.

Boundary: slicer owns `.slicer/relay-roles.json` (`docs/boundaries.md:14`); ork builds the change set and passes it to slicer, never edits the file. Each write lands in the target project's main checkout and stays uncommitted (owner, 2026-10-29, S173 note). A run already started keeps its lineup (`runrec.Record.Lineup`); a launch plan that the copy changes is refused by the `plan changed` check at `run.start`.

Wire (*proposed*, assuming the recommended answers): `matrix.copy {from, to?: [names], all?: bool, dry_run?: bool}`. Exactly one of `to` and `all`. `from` is never a target; `all` means every registered project except `from`. Result `{from, projects: [{project, status, steps?, warnings?, error?}], partial}` where `status` is `would change`, `unchanged`, `changed`, `skipped` or `failed`; `error` is slicer's or ork's code and message unchanged; `partial` is true when some projects changed and some failed.

1. Do not start before the owner has answered Q1-Q8 and S250 has landed with slicer's `relay-roles apply` and its `replace` form released and installed (`slicer --version`). Waits: all questions; the steps below assume the recommendations.

Planner (pure): find the spec-check and UI-pass row ids in both matrices with `SpecCheckRowID` and `UIPassRowID`; build `replace.rows` from the source rows without ids, in source order, with the target's kept rows by id at the places of the source's matching rows (at the end when the source has none); build `replace.rules` as the target's kept rules first, in target order, then the source's other rules without ids, in source order (s444 has no rule move, so kept rules must come first). Handler: resolve `from` and each target with `d.registered`; read both matrices; plan; call `RelayRolesApply` (S250) with `--dry-run` and the rule text not yet rewritten; map each copied source row id to the id the dry run's `add` steps report (check against the landed s444 that its `add` steps keep the order of the rows given; if not, stop and report); rewrite rule text; refuse a copied rule that names a row that is not copied. 7. CLI `ork roles matrix copy FROM (TO... | --all) [--dry-run] [--yes] [--json]`: a dry-run call, the preview, a question per project unless `--yes`, then one write call with the confirmed targets. Waits: Q4, Q7.

9. Do not touch `internal/tui`, `internal/daemon/runs.go` (read `matrixAdapters` only), S173's `matrix.edit`, S250's `matrix.apply` handler, or the matrix of this repository.

## Open owner questions

Open owner questions from the 2026-11-03 spec drafting. Ask the owner before the relay starts; the spec waits on these.

Q1 Source of the unified matrix.
Options: (a) a project named on each call, `ork roles matrix copy FROM ...`, the owner names `ork` (no new state; one extra argument); (b) always the registered project `ork` (shortest command; hard-codes a project name, and the registry name can differ); (c) a master matrix stored by ork, for example in `~/.config/ork/` (one source for all projects; ork then owns matrix data, which needs a new state file in `docs/state.md`, a boundary change against `lineup.source`, and its own editor).
Recommendation: (a).
Waits: wire `from`, Implement step 5.

Q2 What is copied, and replace or merge.
Options: (a) rows and rules, the target replaced except the kept parts of Q3 (true unification; loses each project's own tuning: slicer's `grok-4.7` pins and its parallel-sliver rule u8, adjudicate's u2 and its Sonnet-for-Haiku notes, and ork's ork-specific rules u7 and u10 land in projects they do not describe); (b) rows only, the target's rules kept (rules stay right for each project; rule text that names row ids then points at removed or wrong rows, and ork must warn or refuse); (c) merge: add source rows the target lacks (matched on role, when, agent, model and reasoning), keep the rest (keeps tuning; does not unify; row order decides `recommend`, so where added rows go changes lineups); (d) rows and a named subset of rules (`--rules u1,u3,...`) (precise; the owner picks rule ids per copy).
Recommendation: (a), with Q3's keep list. If the ork-specific rules matter, (d).
Waits: Implement step 4.

Q3 What each target keeps of its own.
Options: (a) its spec-check row and rule, and its UI-pass row and rule if it has one; the source's spec-check and UI-pass rows and rules are not copied; a target without a spec-check rule is refused with `no_spec_check_row` (each project keeps its own spec-check model and UI rule, which names project paths; a copied rule that names a skipped row, as ork's u11 names r14, is refused, so ork's u11 is never copied); (b) copy the source's spec-check and UI-pass rows too, and rewrite their rules to the target's ids (fully uniform; copies ork's UI rule u10 with ork's paths and skills to every project); (c) as (a), but a target without a spec-check rule gets the source's spec-check row and a short rule ork writes, "The spec check before a wave runs the Spec check row (rNN)." (no refusal; ork authors matrix text). Rows for agents ork cannot run (Grok) and row notes are copied as they are in all options, with S250's warning.
Recommendation: (a).
Waits: `TestMatrixCopyPlanTargetWithoutASpecCheckRowIsRefused`, `TestMatrixCopyRefusesACopiedRuleNamingARowThatIsNotCopied`, Implement step 4.

Q4 Dry run and confirmation.
Options: (a) always a dry run first; the CLI shows slicer's steps and the warnings per project and asks `[y/N]` (Enter is No) per project; `--yes` skips the questions for scripts and AI workflows; `--dry-run` stops after the preview; (b) one question for all projects (fewer prompts; one yes changes every project); (c) no question, only `--dry-run` (simplest; a typo writes six projects).
Recommendation: (a).
Waits: `TestRolesMatrixCopyAsksPerProjectAndEnterIsNo`, Implement step 7.

Q5 Apply to all, and a partial failure.
Options: (a) dry-run every target first and write nothing if any dry run fails; then write each target with `expect`, keep going after a write failure (each project is atomic on its own; there is no cross-project rollback), report each project's status, `partial: true`, exit 1; (b) write project by project and stop at the first failure (simple; leaves the rest unchanged and the list half done); (c) write every project that passes, skip the ones that fail, no pre-check (most work done; a typo-level problem in the source is found six times). Projects without a matrix are skipped with the `relay-roles init` hint in all options.
Recommendation: (a).
Waits: `TestMatrixCopyAllChecksEveryProjectBeforeAnyWrite`, `TestMatrixCopyAllReportsAWriteFailureAndGoesOn`, Implement step 5.
